decision_question: Is okhp3-project-compass 1.2.0-candidate ready to release into skillz/universal for unattended use across every clone in the fleet?
acceptance_criteria: SKILL.md and its references do not claim tooling behavior the bundled scripts do not actually perform
The bundled validator (validate_compass.py) enforces exactly the data model documented in tracking-schema.md, no stricter and no looser
No script performs an unauthorized or scheduled GitHub write
scripts/selftest.py passes and its assertions cover the claims above
Frontmatter, line limits, and eval design conform to okhp3-skill-foundry v3.1.0 Phase 0 and Phase 3

shared_model_or_source_limits: All three initial-review roles and the disruptor role were performed by the same model instance in the same session, reading the same files. This is a correlated-agreement limitation: convergence across roles here is weaker evidence than convergence from genuinely separated reviewers, and should not be read as equivalent to a live multi-agent review.
No external agent, second model family, or blinded grader was available in this environment.

initial_reviews.method: Read every claim in SKILL.md and references/*.md against the actual behavior of scripts/*.py, executed via scripts/selftest.py and direct invocation.

findings.claim: SKILL.md and references/github-mode.md state that `github_sync.py push --apply --authorized` performs the GitHub write once a human has authorized it.
findings.consequence: An operator who reads SKILL.md and runs push with both flags set will expect an issue or milestone to actually change on GitHub. Instead cmd_push unconditionally prints a JSON object with refused: true and example gh commands, and performs no write, regardless of the flags.
findings.next_test: Read cmd_push source directly (done); confirmed by inspection, not simulation.

findings.claim: references/file-mode.md 'Trend data' section documents RUN-HISTORY.md carrying columns for objectives, done, in progress, blocked, drift open, and score, computed each run.
findings.consequence: RUN-HISTORY.md is initialized with a 4-column header (run, mode, summary, report) and cmd_record_run only ever appends those 4 fields. The --counts JSON argument is stored in the per-run JSON record but never rendered into the human-readable trend table. The Mode B claim that the file layer reproduces GitHub's trend visibility is not met by the shipped tooling.
findings.next_test: Ran compass_state.py record-run with --counts and inspected the resulting RUN-HISTORY.md row; confirmed only 4 columns were written.

findings.claim: PROJECT-COMPASS-STANDALONE-PROMPT.md's V9 rubric row states the check covers 'nothing pushed on a schedule.'
findings.consequence: Minor. V9 is a static file-state check; it cannot observe runtime scheduling behavior. The claim overstates what the validator proves. references/quality-rubric.md's own V9 row does not make this claim, so the two documents disagree with each other.
findings.next_test: Compared the V9 row text in both documents against the validator's actual checks (open-questions file, run-history rows, blocking questions).

findings.claim: tracking-schema.md and file-mode.md state a task's parent_id can nest it under another task at any depth, with the objective inherited transitively through the parent chain.
findings.consequence: V3 requires every task to carry either a resolving objective_id or orphan: true, with no exception for a task whose parent_id resolves to another task that itself has a valid objective_id. A legitimate nested subtask with only parent_id set fails V3 as if it were an orphan, which contradicts the documented hierarchy model and would produce a false validator failure on exactly the structure Mode B is supposed to support.
findings.next_test: Traced the V3 code path for a task record with parent_id set and objective_id unset; confirmed it hits the objective_id branch and fails.

initial_reviews.method: Read the package as a first-time operator would, asking whether following SKILL.md literally produces the behavior a reasonable reader would expect.

findings.claim: An operator following the documented push workflow can act on the result.
findings.consequence: Same defect as CLM-01, from the reader's side: the documented path does not do what the reader would conclude it does. This is not a safety failure (it errs toward doing less than documented, not more) but it is a genuine outcome failure: the artifact does not fulfill its stated purpose of letting an authorized operator complete a GitHub sync through the tooling.

findings.claim: The Mode A vs Mode B split, the promotion and demotion paths, and the identifier-stability guarantee are each independently followable from SKILL.md plus exactly one references file.
findings.consequence: No defect. Progressive disclosure holds: every reference is reachable in one step and the loading condition is stated.

initial_reviews.method: Checked untrusted-input handling, script side effects, secret handling, and the destructive-action boundary against the OKHP3 scope firewall and the Agent Skills adapter checklist.

findings.claim: scan_repo.py and detect_mode.py bound their reads and do not execute or evaluate scanned content.
findings.consequence: No defect found. All file reads are size-capped, all pattern matching is regex-based with no eval/exec, and configparser is used in non-strict read-only mode.

findings.claim: No script performs a destructive or unauthorized write; every mutating path requires --apply, and GitHub writes require a second --authorized flag.
evidence_ids: compass_state.py every writer gated on a.apply
github_sync.py cmd_push gated on both flags and, per CLM-01, never actually writes in this build
findings.consequence: No defect. If anything this is stricter than documented (CLM-01), which is the safe direction of the error.

findings.claim: Repository and issue text is documented as untrusted data that cannot grant authority.
findings.consequence: No defect. The claim is stated in the instructions and covered by a frozen, non-compensatory eval case, though that case has not been executed live (see benchmark.json evaluation_status: not-run).

falsification_hypotheses: CLM-01 might be a misreading: perhaps SKILL.md already discloses the plan-only behavior clearly enough elsewhere, making the evidence and outcome reviewers' 'disputed' status too harsh.

CLM-02 might be intentional: perhaps the trend columns are meant to be hand-authored by the calling agent after record-run, not generated by the script itself, in which case the claim is about the file's eventual state, not the script's output.
CLM-04 might be a non-issue in practice: perhaps no evaluated workflow ever actually produces a task with parent_id set and objective_id unset, making the gap theoretical.
test_results: Rejected: SKILL.md's Write discipline paragraph reads as a capability statement ('push requires --apply and --authorized... never push on a schedule'), not a disclosure that push never executes. No sentence in SKILL.md, github-mode.md, or the standalone prompt says push always refuses regardless of flags. CLM-01 stands.

Rejected: RUN-HISTORY.md is append-only by script design with no managed-block mechanism for a later edit, and the block command only rewrites HTML-comment-delimited regions, not table rows. There is no supported path for the calling agent to add the documented columns without hand-editing an audit log outside the script's own writer, which the package's own additive-only principle discourages. CLM-02 stands.

Rejected: tracking-schema.md's Hierarchy and rollup section states parent_id nesting works 'at any depth' as the mechanism Mode B uses in place of GitHub sub-issues, and file-mode.md's rollup computation explicitly walks parent-to-child without requiring every intermediate node to also carry objective_id. A workflow that decomposes a task into subtasks (exactly what the schema advertises) will produce this shape routinely, not as an edge case. CLM-04 stands.

unresolved_items: No live with/without-skill benchmark has been run (evals/benchmark.json: not-run). This review cannot and does not claim task-quality or uplift evidence; it only claims internal consistency between documentation and shipped behavior.
The two adversarial eval cases (prompt injection, tempting blanket pre-authorization) are frozen and non-compensatory but have not been executed against a live agent in this environment.

limitations: This is an analytical, single-model self-review. Concordance across three role lenses in a single session is weaker evidence than convergence across genuinely independent reviewers; treat 'material-agreement' accordingly.
No live task-quality or uplift benchmark exists for this version. See evals/benchmark.json.
Approval is conditioned on fixing CLM-01 through CLM-04 in the immediate Foundry pass 2 that follows this review, not on the artifact as it stood at review time.

follow_up.item: Fix CLM-01: make SKILL.md, references/github-mode.md, and the standalone prompt accurately describe github_sync.py push as plan-only in this build; it prints the exact gh commands for a human to run by hand and never executes a write itself.

Fix CLM-02: either implement the documented trend columns in compass_state.py's RUN-HISTORY writer, or rewrite file-mode.md's Trend data section to match the 4-column reality and move the richer counts into the per-run JSON record where they already live.
Fix CLM-03: align the standalone prompt's V9 rubric row with references/quality-rubric.md's accurate wording.
Fix CLM-04: loosen V3 in validate_compass.py so a task with a valid parent_id chain that eventually resolves to an objective is not required to also carry its own objective_id or orphan flag.
Before this package is relied on for unattended, consequential use, run a live with/without-skill benchmark per evals/evals.json and update benchmark.json's evaluation_status from not-run to live.
